column7: Typo – The Window Display explicitly prints `kaśalī`. The canonical text of *Raghuvaṃśa* 5.4 strictly dictates the word **`kuśalī`** (the nominative singular of the masculine possessive adjective `kuśalin`, meaning healthy, safe, or prosperous). The printed `kaśalī` is a typographical corruption, substituting the foundational vowel *u* with an *a*, thereby destroying the structural and semantic integrity of the word.

column7: Typo – this is a corrupt reading for the canonical `kuru`. `kuru` is the imperative mood (loṭ), parasmaipada, second-person singular of the verbal root `kṛ` (to do / to make). It operates as the principal verb commanding the action of the clause.
